text.p: Two of Germany's largest commercial banks, Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypobank will merge, Vereinsbank said on Monday, announcing a move set to change the German banking landscape.

Merger proceedings between the two Bavarian banks will start in October. Vereinsbank said in a regulatory statement that the new bank would be called Bayerische Hypo-und Vereinsbank, adding the merger would ultimately bring savings of about one billion marks per year.

Vereinsbank said it would take up to 45 percent of Hypobank stock in advance of the merger and would offer Hypobank shareholders shares in the insurance giant Allianz AG, where they will receive one Allianz share for six Hypobank shares.
The merger will lead to clearly higher earnings per share (EPS) and Vereinsbank said it expected restructuring costs to total around 1.3 billion marks.
Vereinsbank said that the two banks would hold a news conference at 0900 GMT.
